description:
Deferred non-blocking follow-up from the retention-floor work (bead pqueue-b5cc2bc7), noted in crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs branch_with_emission. Branch creation is atomic via a commit marker (branch.json written LAST) + a branch.pending sentinel; an uncommitted branch is non-readable, so a partial/failed branch is safe (never reads a reclaimed segment). BUT a failed branch creation (or a rollback whose object cleanup itself failed) can leave ORPHAN objects on the store: a leftover branch.pending sentinel and/or partially-copied branch manifest/segment objects. These are harmless (non-readable, do not corrupt) but they are durable garbage that is never reclaimed — a slow space leak proportional to failed-branch-creation attempts.

SCOPE: implement GC for orphaned/uncommitted-branch objects — a branch whose commit marker (branch.json) is ABSENT but whose sentinel/objects are present, past a safety window, can have ALL its objects (sentinel, manifest, segments, floor entries) deleted. Must be safe: never delete objects of a COMMITTED branch (marker present) or an in-flight creation still within its window; coordinate with the branch pin so a live source pin from an in-flight creation is respected.

acceptance: 1. lease_decide_acquire preserves assignment_epoch when acquiring owner == current.active_owner; bumps only on different/none owner. 2. description: Under CPU starvation / high host load, multi-node object_log_sqlite_projection collapses ~36x (8-owner worst per-queue 3300/s -> 87/s) instead of degrading gracefully. ROOT CAUSE (code-traced): each node runs its own InMemoryControlPlane (sole owner of its disjoint queues). When the background renew_sessions task runs late under load, the lease TTL (15s) lapses; cp_resolve reports Unassigned; the node re-acquires via lease_decide_acquire (control_plane.rs:126) which UNCONDITIONALLY does assignment_epoch+1. That epoch bump fences the node's OWN in-flight pushes/claims (EpochFenced / -ERR pqueue epoch_stale) -> client retry storm -> under continued starvation repeats -> collapse. A slow-but-alive owner fences itself. FIX: re-affirming ownership of one's OWN uncontested lease (current.active_owner == acquiring owner) must PRESERVE assignment_epoch (refresh lease_expires_at only); epoch advances ONLY on takeover by a DIFFERENT owner. Safe: if the authority record still names us active_owner, no other owner acquired in the gap. Result: graceful degradation. Exposed by pqueue-36d405a9's live cargo test failing its 8-owner sweep under host load ~13 on a 12-core box.
title: Ownership self-fencing under load: re-acquiring own lease bumps the fence epoch (no graceful degradation)

description:
PROBLEM: A composition pairing an S3-backed object log with a PostgreSQL projection can never be opened. Every attempt fails at backend open with "invalid: schema name must be [A-Za-z0-9_]". Reported by snorri (snorri-b4e19d55), reproduced 2026-07-22 against Garage v2.2.0 + postgres:16-alpine in Kind at pqueue v0.19.4 (982adcb9).

ROOT CAUSE: One string serves two incompatible roles. The embedded durability config carries a single `namespace`, which pqueue uses BOTH to scope the S3 object-log keys AND as the PostgreSQL schema name for the projection. Callers must therefore satisfy the intersection of "legal S3 key prefix" and "legal SQL identifier", which is not achievable in practice: snorri synthesizes `snorri-s3-v1:{prefix_len}:{key_prefix}{namespace}` (snorri crates/snorri-embed/src/lib.rs:1019), whose literal prefix alone contains `-` and `:`. The value also routinely exceeds the 63-byte PostgreSQL identifier limit (~100 chars in the observed case), so quoting the identifier is not sufficient on its own.

Never caught because the combination is untested on either side: pqueue exercises the Postgres object-log path only with ObjectLogAdapterStorage::Local, and snorri's objectlog-s3 feature force-enables sqlite rather than postgres.

PROPOSED FIX: Derive the PostgreSQL schema name inside pqueue instead of using the caller namespace verbatim. Keep `namespace` unchanged as the S3 object-log key scope, and map it to a bounded, deterministic [A-Za-z0-9_] identifier (e.g. a stable hash rendered as `pq_<hex>`) that respects the 63-byte limit.

This is the only option that requires no migration. In this composition PostgreSQL holds a DISPOSABLE projection, not the authoritative log (the authority is the S3 object log; snorri exposes delete_projection()/rehydrate() for exactly this), so the schema name is not a durable lineage identifier here and renaming it is safe. No S3+Postgres deployment can exist today because the composition has never opened. Re-encoding the namespace itself was rejected: it would relocate existing S3+SQLite object-log data and require a migration.

NON-SCOPE: Do not change the namespace value passed for S3 object-log key scoping, and do not alter S3+SQLite lineage or layout. Do not change the schema semantics of composed_postgres_backend_in_schema, where the caller-supplied schema IS the durable log and reconnecting with the same schema must keep reopening it. Do not weaken the existing schema-name validation for callers that legitimately supply an identifier directly.
title: postgres: derive a legal schema name instead of using the caller namespace verbatim

description:
PROBLEM: Partial expiry needs a visibility rule that distinguishes durable manifest deletion completion from ordinary read-horizon advancement. Without an explicit decision state, a future manifest deletion pass can make below-floor segment entries disappear from enumeration before their segment objects are durably reclaimed. Governing artifact: docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:370 and docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:374. Dependency ID: pqueue-8928baec. Depends on child bead `objectlog: persist durable manifest deletion watermark for below-floor reclamation`. Parent: pqueue-b5c4d46d. Parent tracker: pqueue-bc67f1b5.
ROOT CAUSE: crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:1367 reads the current read horizon directly for manifest enumeration, crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:1384 loads the cached manifest deletion watermark from the same read-horizon source, and crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:2769 derives a new watermark from reclaimed progress; these paths do not expose one internal visibility decision object that can say an undeleted below-floor segment remains visible while partial reclamation is active.
PROPOSED FIX: Introduce an internal partial-expire visibility state or equivalent helper that combines the durable manifest deletion watermark, the caller's active reclaimed-through boundary, and the current retention floor. Route manifest enumeration decisions used by read/recovery/expiry through that helper so entries above the durable watermark remain visible, and entries below a partial reclaimed-through boundary are hidden only when proven reclaimed. Keep the helper internal and behavior-compatible with existing live/read-horizon enumeration.
NON-SCOPE: Do not implement the main manifest deletion pass in this bead except for controlled fixtures needed to simulate partial progress. Do not alter branch pin rules or delete branch-pinned source segments. Do not hide not-yet-deleted below-floor segments during partial expiry. Do not change request-id retention, client item-key retention, terminal retention, or projection storage. Do not implement a delete-only compaction on the current index-CAS protocol. Do not drop legacy manifest bootstrap support until an explicit migration bead exists.

description:
PROBLEM: After pqueue-8be1206b (v0.19.6) fixed the schema-name rejection, snorri integrated v0.19.6 and found that an S3 object log with a PostgreSQL projection still cannot be used. Two further defects sit behind the one that was fixed. Verified 2026-07-22 against Garage v2.2.0 + postgres:16-alpine, pqueue v0.19.6 (90772fb7), snorri at the v0.19.6 bump.

DEFECT 1 -- embedded Postgres projection advertises no commit capabilities. For the SAME S3 object log, an embedded composition with a SQLite projection satisfies snorri CONTRACT-003, while a Postgres projection reports: missing=[AtomicTransitionCommit,VectorizedTransitionCommit,ClaimLeaseValidation,RetainedCommitIdempotency,AuthoritativeRecoveryReads], durability=EventualApply, consistency=None, transport=SingularFallback, max_batch_size=10000. These values come from Pqueue::commit_capabilities(probe_key), which returns Ok with every flag false rather than EngineError::Unavailable, so it is a genuine capability report and not a probe failure. The object log is the authority in both cases, so the commit-capability profile should not depend on which disposable projection backend is attached.

DEFECT 2 -- the embedded Postgres open path blocks inside an async runtime. open_embedded -> PostgresRelational::connect_in_schema uses the synchronous postgres client, which calls block_on internally. Invoked from a thread already driving a tokio runtime it panics with "Cannot start a runtime from within a runtime" (postgres-0.19.14/src/config.rs:465). The equivalent SQLite path composes cleanly from the same async context. pqueue tests only exercise this from sync #[test] bodies using futures::executor::block_on, so the hazard is invisible upstream, but embedders compose inside an async main.

Note: the S3 + Postgres coverage added in pqueue-8be1206b (public_s3_objectlog_postgres_open_and_reopen_with_disposable_projection) skips unless PQUEUE_S3_TEST_URL is set, so neither defect is caught by a default run.

PROPOSED FIX: (1) Derive the commit-capability profile for embedded compositions from the authoritative object log rather than the projection backend, so SQLite and Postgres projections over one object log report the same profile. acceptance: 1. Manifest OBJECT COUNT (not just read cost) is bounded on a long-lived trimmed queue: below-floor manifest objects are physically reclaimed, keeping total manifest objects ~O(live)+O(recent-history). 2. The cross-owner stale-writer fence is PRESERVED without relying on the write-once index address space: a superseded/stale writer can never false-ack a phantom entry (proven by an adversarial test interleaving a compaction/deletion with a stale-epoch writer's commit). 3. AC-TXN-3 replay-across-restart, behind-image fail-closed, branch inheritance, and the retention floor all still hold. 4. Codex adversarial review APPROVES the new fencing/commit protocol. 5. rustup 1.92.0 cargo test across objectlog+sqlite+engine+conformance passes; fmt + clippy -D warnings clean.
description: Deferred Option 2 from the manifest-compaction design (bead pqueue-8928baec, closed; see docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md). The shipped read-horizon fix (pqueue-8928baec) bounds per-READ/recovery cost to live history but deliberately NEVER frees a manifest index address (the write-once put_if_absent index collision is the only stale-writer fence, and writer staleness is unbounded at the substrate), so manifest OBJECT COUNT + storage bytes still grow slowly as never-read below-horizon entries. Erik accepted that residual for now (read-cost was the operational pain). This bead is the larger change to bound object COUNT: replace the per-index-collision fence with a redesigned atomic fencing/commit protocol so manifest indices CAN be physically deleted safely — e.g. a PERMANENT linearizable head object (current epoch + next index) updated via conditional-update/CAS as the fence, plus UNIQUE per-attempt segment keys so a rolled-back/stale write cannot resurrect or clobber a live segment. That decouples the fence from the index address space, allowing true deletion of below-floor manifest objects (bounding read AND storage). HIGH blast radius: touches the core commit path (seal), recover_manifest (read head instead of list-max), branch manifest copy, epoch fencing, and needs a new BlobStore conditional-head primitive; own release + multi-round codex hardening. Only pursue if manifest object-count/storage growth becomes operationally real (very long-lived, high-write, trimming-enabled queues). Related root cause: pqueue ownership fence wiring (the c33c367e follow-up) — if a superseded owner were provably fenced within a bounded window < retention_ms, a cheaper delete-only compaction might become viable; evaluate that interaction first.
title: objectlog: bound manifest OBJECT COUNT via a fencing/commit-protocol redesign (compaction Option 2)

PROPOSED FIX: add an explicit full-width PQUEUE_OWNER_ID runtime setting, validate it with OwnerId rules, require it when PQUEUE_REPLICA_COUNT>1, carry it through Config/start/run_owned, and retain PQUEUE_NODE_ID only for existing item/command ID behavior. description:

Depends on child bead `objectlog: persist durable manifest deletion watermark for below-floor reclamation` and the eligibility child bead from this decomposition. ROOT CAUSE: crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:1996 states that expire_segments_through deletes only segment objects; crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:1998 deliberately does not delete manifest tombstones; docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:370 records the residual that object count still grows because addresses are never freed.

NON-SCOPE: Do not introduce the durable manifest deletion watermark in this bead; consume the watermark from its dependency. Do not define new watermark advancement semantics beyond calling the dependency-provided API after successful deletion progress. Do not alter branch pin rules or delete branch-pinned source segments. Do not implement a delete-only compaction on the current index-CAS protocol. Do not drop legacy manifest bootstrap support until an explicit migration bead exists.
title: objectlog: physically delete eligible below-floor manifest objects during expiry

acceptance: 1. A restart test uses a durable SQLite-backed server/backend, advances the storage fence above genesis, recreates the in-memory ownership control plane, and proves the queue can be safely reacquired and serve a real push/claim. 2. The reacquired owner's storage fence is strictly safe against the pre-restart owner's cached epoch; stale push/claim/finalize are EpochFenced and current-owner operations succeed. 3. The solution distinguishes ephemeral reset control planes from durable/transactionally-bound control planes and does not turn current_epoch > assignment_epoch into an unconditional accept. 4. description: The disposition landed by pqueue-7bac12ce incorrectly claims the two-counter lease/storage fence gap is benign for SQLite compositions because the in-memory control plane resets on process restart. In production run_owned uses a fresh InMemoryControlPlane while durable backends retain their storage epoch. After a restart, acquire_queue_lease starts again at assignment_epoch=1 while backend.current_epoch may be greater; acquire_and_fence and OwnershipRuntime::acquire_queue currently return EpochFenced when current_epoch > assignment_epoch, leaving the queue permanently unacquirable. Reconcile the reset lease epoch with the durable storage fence without allowing a superseded owner to write at a reused fence. Preserve separate lease_epoch and fence_epoch semantics and fail closed for genuinely inconsistent durable control planes.
title: ownership: reconcile reset lease epochs with durable storage fences on restart

description: Residual from pqueue-48a4af85 / commit aec2f3f5. rebuild_commit_idempotency_from_log reconstructs commit_transition's commit_idempotency cache from the durable log, but a REJECTED entry mutates nothing and appends nothing durable, so a commit that mixed committed+rejected entries reconstructs ONLY its committed, Finalize-delimited entries — a shorter Vec<EntryRecovery> than the live record. This is currently SAFE (not silently replayed): commit_transition's replay path guards on recovery.len()==entries.len(), so a short reconstructed record falls through to 0-duplicate re-execution rather than returning a misleading short outcome vec (committed inputs stay finalized exactly once). But it is NOT a faithful replay of the original per-entry vec. The full fix requires durably recording per-entry REJECTION outcomes on the commit (a wire-format / error-serialization change deliberately deferred from aec2f3f5 as pre-release risk, since it touches the shared CommandEnvelope across all backend crates). Also affects explain_commit, which returns only the committed subset for a reconstructed mixed commit.
title: AC-TXN-3 residual: faithful mixed committed+rejected commit_transition replay across restart (durable rejection records)

description:

Add regression coverage for a pass that fails after deleting an earlier segment but before deleting a later below-floor segment, then verify retry enumeration still sees the undeleted later segment. description:
PROBLEM
Partial expiry needs a manifest deletion watermark that is independent from the read horizon. Advancing manifest deletion state based only on logical expiry can hide below-floor manifest entries that were not physically deleted, which breaks later full expiry and recovery. Governing artifact: docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:370 and docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:374. Dependency ID: pqueue-8928baec. crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:1996 states that expire_segments_through deletes only segment objects. crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:1998 deliberately does not delete manifest tombstones. crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:2028 advances only the read horizon after reclamation. Without separate conservative manifest deletion bookkeeping, partial expiry can move manifest visibility past below-floor entries that are still present and still needed by later expiry or recovery.

PROPOSED FIX
Introduce persisted or reconstructable manifest deletion watermark bookkeeping that is separate from the read horizon. The watermark must advance only through a contiguous prefix of manifest objects that are physically deleted, unpinned, and below the expiry floor. Wire the new state into expiry metadata without changing branch pin semantics or legacy bootstrap behavior.

NON-SCOPE

Do not change request-id retention, client item-key retention, terminal retention, or projection storage. Do not implement a delete-only compaction on the current index-CAS protocol. PROBLEM: `acquire_epoch` must participate in the same permanent head-CAS fence as `seal`; otherwise a new owner can start writing data before the durable head reflects ownership, leaving stale old-epoch or future-epoch appends insufficiently fenced. Governing artifact: docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:359 and docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:374. Dependency ID: pqueue-8928baec; evaluate pqueue-c33c367e owner-fence wiring before implementation and document whether it can bound stale writers inside retention.
ROOT CAUSE: crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:1264 fences only against the in-memory `buf.committed_epoch`; crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:1281 writes deterministic segment keys from `first_seq`; crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:1300 commits via `put_if_absent` at `manifest/{cur_index}`; crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:1302 handles CAS loss by rereading the manifest tail. docs/perf/design/manifest-compaction-hotpath.md:359 rejects tail-validate rollback because deterministic segment keys and reader-visible manifest commits make rollback unsafe.
PROPOSED FIX: Redesign `acquire_epoch` so the permanent manifest head is advanced as the ownership fence before the new owner can write data. Preserve rejection of stale old-epoch and invalid future-epoch appends as `EpochFenced`, and keep the protocol compatible with the unique attempt segment key scheme used by `seal`.

Do not change projection apply semantics, request-id replay, branch creation, retention policy, or release packaging. Do not accept tail-validate/delete rollback as a substitute for head CAS. Do not rely on pqueue-c33c367e unless this bead proves and documents the bounded-window invariant.
title: objectlog: make acquire_epoch advance the permanent head fence
